title: OKFM 0.2.1 configuration
description: Generated from dropin/config_schema.py — do not edit by hand. `dev/check_schema.py` fails when this file and that table disagree.

okfm.description: Which OKFM profile this config is written against.

pack.description: Path to a domain pack directory, or null for none. The key must be present even when empty — a mesh with no domain is a normal mesh, not a missing answer. A path rather than a bare name (DR-0014): a name needs a search order, and a search order picks the wrong directory silently.

root.description: The folder to read. Every subfolder of documents under it becomes a bundle.

root_files.description: Turn the documents sitting directly in the root into their own bundle. Set false when they are a landing page and two stubs rather than knowledge.

exclude.description: Subtrees to skip, relative to the root. An archive of superseded documents is the usual first entry.

include.description: Folders outside the root to read as well, relative to the project. This is the only way to reach one; nothing scans your project on its own.

out.description: Where bundles are written. Your documents are never written to.

mesh.description: The generated OKF whose concepts are the other OKFs — the one to read first.

mode.description: mirror writes concepts beside your files and never touches them. The only mode: for a folder whose documents ARE the concepts, add the frontmatter yourself and name it in `bundles` — the build registers it and writes nothing into it.

vocab_overlays.description: Extra pack DIRECTORIES, for a mesh drawing on more than one. Each family reads only the file bearing its own name — predicates.yaml, types.yaml, reason_codes.yaml, roles.yaml — so a pack cannot widen a list it did not mean to. Usually empty; `pack` covers the single-domain case.

bundle_tags.description: bundle id → tags every concept the build writes there carries. For claims that belong to the folder rather than to any one file — every component in a level-2 bundle is `needs-nothing` by definition, and extraction cannot read that off prose. A tag added by hand to a build-owned concept is erased on the next run, so the build has to be the thing that knows.

sources.description: An explicit list of folders. Its presence turns discovery off entirely — somebody who wrote one meant it.

bundles.description: id → path. Its presence turns discovery off. The id should be the folder name: two names for one bundle means the second one exists to be got wrong.

path.description: The single-file viewer. Opens from disk; there is no server.

index.description: Where the generated index is written, if you want it as a separate file.

serve_port.description: Port for the optional local preview. Not needed to open the file.

max_concepts.description: How many concepts an injected index may carry before it costs more than it buys.

priority_types.description: Types that survive the budget first, most important first.

exclude_scopes.description: Scopes kept out of health statistics and out of any context assembled for an agent — the bundled guide is the usual entry.

enabled.description: Turn on Level 2+ — OKFM drafts descriptions itself, using a model on hardware you control. Off by default: nothing should start calling a model because a config file mentioned one.

base_url.description: Where Ollama answers. http://localhost:11434 when it runs on this machine; http://<host>:11434 for a box on your network — that host needs OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0 to accept anything but its own loopback.

model.description: The model tag to draft with. It must ALREADY be pulled on that Ollama instance — nothing here downloads it. Avoid reasoning models: thinking is disabled, and one that ignores that spends minutes per concept.

num_ctx.description: Tokens the model may hold. Ollama defaults to 2048, which silently truncates a long document and describes only the half it saw.

timeout_s.description: How long to wait for one answer. A small model on a CPU is slow, not stuck.

stores.description: External data stores. Credentials are named by handle and never written here: a config file is committed, a credential is not.

registry.description: The bundle that registers the others. null is a valid mesh — a registry appears when a second owner does.

$schema.description: Path to this schema, so an editor validates the file as you type. Nothing in OKFM reads it.
